answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by gating identity on provably costly work. To register, an agent solves a unique cipher puzzle and stakes collateral locked for an epoch. A farm creating ten thousand fake peers pays that cost ten thousand times, while an honest agent pays once. Staked reputation is anchored to on-chain history, so clones start empty and cannot inherit trust. Honest nodes use shared funding and attestation graphs to harbor the network against fake voting blocs. The stake is a basalt base: visible and costly to haul, so minting fakes costs more than they earn.
